source.title: The Safety Gap Toolkit: Evaluating Hidden Dangers of Open-Source Models
source.authors: Ann-Kathrin Dombrowski; Dillon Bowen; Adam Gleave; Chris Cundy

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study applies refusal ablation on open-weight instruct models. It computes per-layer harmful-versus-harmless activation differences and orthogonalizes model weights, then measures compliance with harmful requests and benign response quality. This is a direct application of the original refusal-ablation method on additional models.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own refusal-ablation outcomes in Tables 2–3. It also describes the procedure and cites claims about refusal directions, but results cited from other work are not included as rows. It does not report adding a direction, harmless-request refusal rates after addition, or attack suppression of the direction.
record.test_reason: The study applies the original difference-in-means refusal ablation, as a weight orthogonalization, to 9 released Llama-3 and Qwen2.5 instruct models. It reports harmful-request compliance (StrongREJECT judge) and capability and quality before and after ablation (Tables 2–3). These are direct results on whether ablation removes refusal while preserving abilities (V1) and whether the weight edit works on released models (V2). Refusal ablation is a borrowed technique in their toolkit, not their own method, so this is not T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add the paper's headline: the safety gap widens with model scale, and safeguards (including via refusal ablation) are removed with minimal compute while WMDP knowledge is unchanged. On ablation specifically: compliance rises sharply, and quality is preserved better than with fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper describes refusal ablation as computing per-layer harmful-versus-harmless activation differences, selecting a direction based on refusal rate and harmless-prompt KL, and orthogonalizing weight matrices. It evaluates this weight-edit form on Llama-3 and Qwen2.5 instruct models.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and harmful-request domain. The method failed to identify a suitable direction for Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, and the authors could not produce a high-quality ablated Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct. Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct had notably elevated baseline compliance.
record.problems: The paper states that refusal ablation could not be evaluated for Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct or Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct. The capability evidence is limited to WMDP accuracy and 100 Freebase QA questions, rather than a broad general-capability suite. The paper reports 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for bar plots, but table values do not provide uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: The table reports chemistry and cyber WMDP accuracy for the ablated and original models, but those rows were omitted to remain within the 60-row limit after retaining all reported harmful-request compliance domains and the WMDP-Bio and benign-quality capability checks. Chemistry and cyber WMDP accuracy values are in Appendix A.3, Tables 2–3.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests is not tested. Capability preservation is checked only with WMDP multiple-choice accuracy and 100 Freebase QA questions.
No models beyond Llama-3 and Qwen2.5 instruct. Llama-3.1-405B could not be ablated for hardware and quantization reasons, which says nothing on the claim.

missing.what: Refusal ablation failed for Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct: no candidate direction gave both refusal separation and small harmless-prompt KL. No ablation results are reported for it.

record.verdict_notes: Toolkit paper; refusal ablation is one of two safeguard-removal methods. Removal is clearly weaker in the smallest Llama models, which the authors do not discuss; their text says models comply with 'up to 95%' of requests. WMDP chem/cyber rows are declared in rows_left_out and are likewise unchanged. No uncertainty is given in the tables. The baseline-compliance differences (e.g. Llama-3.3-70B at 0.18) do not affect the verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests ablation and reports harmful-request compliance plus capability-related measures. It does not test adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests, and its capability checks are WMDP accuracy and Freebase QA response quality rather than a comprehensive assessment of other abilities.
Tests weight-based refusal ablation on several released instruct models. It does not test every released model or establish performance on models for which ablation could not be produced.
The study does not test attacks that suppress the direction or training against ablation.
The study does not compare a single direction with an affine subspace, cone, or multiple directions.
The study does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
The study does not test transfer across languages, base/instruct variants, or other transfer settings.

The study does not compare how or when refusal training was applied. It reports that ablation could not identify a suitable direction for Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, but does not investigate training as the cause.
The study does not evaluate reasoning models or test whether the claim holds for them.

relation.reason: Reports compliance before and after the ablation on 9 models, plus WMDP accuracy and Freebase QA quality: direct results on whether ablation and the weight edit remove refusal while keeping capability.

tranche.reason: Same difference-in-means direction, selection by refusal rate plus a harmless-prompt KL constraint, and the original weight orthogonalization (cites Arditi Section C). It measures harmful compliance and capability before and after.

source_check.notes: Compliance is judged by the StrongREJECT evaluator on the authors' propensity sets (283 bio, 312 chem, 516 cyber questions). There is no random-direction control; table values have no CIs (the figures give bootstrap 95% CIs). Section 4.2 says removal reaches 'up to 95%' compliance while Table 2 gives 0.98-1.00; the rows follow the tables. Qwen2.5-1.5B baselines are already 0.58-0.75. Llama-3.1-405B was not ablated (hardware/quantization), so no >100B result.

statements.correction: Named models: ablated compliance 0.98-1.00 on bio/chem/cyber (Tables 2-3); Llama-3.1-8B bio 0.00->0.98. WMDP-Bio and Freebase QA quality change by at most 0.01. Judge: StrongREJECT evaluator on the authors' Bio-Chem-Cyber Propensity sets. Nine ablated instruct models; code on GitHub.
statements.problem: For the models it names (Llama-3.1-8B/70B, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-7B/32B/72B), compliance is 0.98-1.00, not 0.90-1.00; the 0.90 floor comes from Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-3.2-3B, which are not named. The conditions list 'propensity datasets' as a judge; this study's judge is the StrongREJECT evaluator.

statements.correction: Llama-3.2-1B: 0.67/0.61/0.71 (bio/chem/cyber). Llama-3.2-3B: 0.85/0.75/0.90. Llama-3.1-8B: 0.98/0.99/0.98. Weight orthogonalization, StrongREJECT-judged propensity compliance (Table 2).
statements.problem: Minor: Llama-3.1-8B ablated compliance is 0.98-0.99, not 0.98-1.00. The Llama-3.2-1B and 3B ranges are right.

statements.correction: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct weight edit: bio 0.03->0.85, chem 0.05->0.75, cyber 0.03->0.90 (Table 2); incomplete removal compared with 0.98-1.00 in models of 8B and up.
statements.problem: Llama-3.2-3B's chem baseline is 0.05, not 0.03. The statement lists this study under 'Strong' removal, but 0.75-0.90 compliance (10-25% residual refusal) is what the record's own V1/V2 limits_scope verdicts treat as partial.

statements.correction: Appendix A.2: no high-quality refusal-ablated Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct; Section 4 attributes this to the toolkit not supporting quantized or multi-node models on 8xH100.

statements.problem: The visible (truncated) text says nothing about this study and no rows are cited, so the claim about it can't be checked.
Minor: 0.19->0.99 (r12) is cyber and 0.18->0.99 (r13) is bio; domains are not labelled.
Accurate, but it omits that within this study Llama-3.2-3B cyber reached 0.90 and Qwen2.5-1.5B (also 3B or under) reached 0.90-0.97.
